prompt:
Task: HD remaster of a sheet of animation frames from the 1995 adventure game The Dig (LucasArts), in the smooth, detailed style approved for the main characters. This is a production asset. Every frame is fitted to the original frame's size and position afterwards, and the game lays it over the HD background with its own soft edges.

Input: the attached image is the original low-resolution sheet enlarged 4x with hard pixel edges. The frames stand apart on a plain flat cyan background (#00C8C8). Around the sheet is a plain gray (#808080) border. The border is only padding.

All frames on this sheet are animation frames of the same characters (Boston Low and Ludger Brink), as one scene, in different poses. On this sheet, row by row from left to right: start pose, facing right (1 frame); animation 7, facing right (16 frames).

Do:
- Repaint every frame in high resolution with clean, natural detail: smooth shading instead of dithering, smooth anti-aliased outlines (no pixel steps), believable cloth, skin, hair and material.
- Keep the original look: the same character, the same colors, light direction, shadows and contrast, in the painted style of the approved HD sheets.
- Make all frames look identical apart from the pose: the same face, hair, clothes, colors and light in every frame. The frames are played one after another in the game, so any difference between them flickers.
- Keep the pose, proportions and silhouette of every frame as in the input, and keep each frame in its place on the sheet, in the same rows and the same order.
- Glowing effects (light, energy, lightning, sparks) are painted as soft glow that fades into transparency.

Do not:
- Do not add, remove, merge or redesign frames. Do not add anything between the frames: no shadows, floor, text, numbers, labels, frames or grid lines.
- Do not let frames touch or overlap each other.
- Some frames show only part of the character, for example a body without a head or a head alone, because the game draws the parts separately. Paint them as they are and do not complete them.
- Small bright magenta marks under the feet or at the edges are shadow markers used by the game. Leave them out; the game draws the shadow itself.
- No photorealism, no modern 3D look, no film grain, no vignette, no watermark, no signature.

Output: one PNG image, exactly 1536 x 1024 pixels, with a fully transparent background (real alpha, no background color and no gray border) and the frames in the same layout as the input. List the delivery with its sha256 in the fremdrift.json of your report and add a rutekart (the box around each frame's drawing) as for the main characters.

If a second image is attached, it is an already approved HD sheet of the same character, or an approved HD picture from the same game. Paint the character exactly as in that image: the same face, hair, clothes, colors and level of detail. Take all poses and the layout from the first image.


TOM-AUTHORIZED PRECISE CHARACTER/SOURCE CORRECTION:
Image1 is the ORIGINAL costume174 sheet and absolute authority for every pose, part, color, lighting state and animation sequence. Image2 is Tom's approved plain BOSTON LOW FACE/SMOOTH DRAWN IDENTITY crop, from the approved smooth walking test: use his square angular jaw, long cheek plane, dark short brown hair with pronounced gray temple side, straight nose, small mouth, clean dark drawn contours and angular flat shaded color planes. Its warm healthy skin and background are not this source variant's palette. Image3 is an original-RGBA MAIN-SPRITE-ONLY diagnostic count/pose guide, same exact row order as image1. Its labels and gray backing are diagnostics and must not appear in the output. These explicit image roles override the generic base-reference description.
ACTUAL SHEET CONTENT: Although costume174's broad metadata names Boston and Brink, this particular sheet shows ONLY BOSTON LOW. He is the brown-haired man in a PLAIN DARK NAVY/TEAL SHORT-SLEEVE T-SHIRT, no jacket, no chest badge, burnt dark ochre/brown trousers, black-blue boots. Preserve this exact original outfit. Do not convert him to blond Brink or add Brink's gray jacket. No helmet, backpack, spacesuit or gloves. His exposed forearms stay bare.
SOURCE LIGHTING: costume174 is under subdued olive/green ambient light. Preserve image1's muted olive-tan exposed skin and brown/olive dark hair, very dark navy shirt, dark brown-ochre trousers and blue-black boots. Actual head source highlights are muted olive-tan roughly RGB139,127,67, with ochre-brown shadows, not bright peach skin. The approved face ref controls identity/drawn style only; its healthy peach palette does not override this actual green-lit source state. No neon green skin, plastic highlights, white sleeve stripes or arbitrary resurrection damage. Smooth natural drawn shadow planes, no photographic grain or3D rendering.
EXACT MAIN ROWS: top row1 complete Boston standing, middle row10 complete Boston frames, bottom row5 complete Boston frames. Total16 main figures. Every main figure is headed and fully dressed exactly as source; no loose heads or completed fragments. Keep original source frame order, head tilts, leaning/arm differences, fixed skull/neck scale and original feet baselines. Do not replace the sixteen different source poses with clones.
In the later middle-row frames his visible hand and the tiny pale gray/white curved jagged artifact begin to emerge; in bottom row it is gradually lifted. Copy each source phase exactly, including the original small irregular pale shape, bare hand/finger placement and its size. It is not a big glowing sphere, full ring, glove, weapon or invented item. No glow outside the source shape and no new prop in earlier empty-hand frames. Top and first seven middle frames have no invented white prop. The middle-row slot8 has only its tiny original pale sliver; slots9/10 and the five bottom frames follow their distinct visible source artifact/hand shape.
One genuine single dark original pixel costume174_054 has RGBA[7,11,19,255] and is already retained through original-RGBA import fallback. It is not a head, hand or shadow marker, and must not be expanded into an extra native object. Image3 omits only this true fallback fragment. Total native main16, exact rows[1,10,5].
Keep every real limb, prop and source detail; omit only bright magenta technical footmarks. Native complete1536x1024 RGBA sheet with true transparent background, smooth antialiased edges and clear separation. No cyan/gray field, vignette, matte, floor, cast shadows, text, digits, frame outlines, grid, watermark or marks between figures. Do not crop any head, hand or boot.

SPECIFIC DRAWN STYLE AND SOURCE COLOR ENFORCEMENT: The whole sheet, including skin, shirt, trousers and boots, uses reference2's clean 2D drawn contours and angular distinct cel-painted shadow planes with smooth edges. Avoid round airbrushed/plastic3D surface volume or photographic/3D-game rendering. Match the approved drawn face silhouette and pronounced gray sideburn/temple. Apply the source174 olive-green-lit skin, not the healthy orange skin of the style crop. Actual costume174_001 trouser source colors (diagnostic original-RGBA) are [{'rgb': [95, 51, 7], 'hex': '#5F3307', 'pixels': 166}, {'rgb': [115, 63, 0], 'hex': '#733F00', 'pixels': 159}, {'rgb': [75, 35, 0], 'hex': '#4B2300', 'pixels': 73}]. Preserve this dark source family rather than bright orange from another costume. The held pale artifact is a small irregular pale gray/white curved source shape, not shiny sculpted chrome or a luminous large ring. Keep its exact changing source contour and relative size. Native rows remain exactly[1,10,5], total16 fully headed Boston bodies, no helmets or other figures.
